items.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: we started to hang out. I started going to his house and everything else... I got to know him

ctx.x: I was going to ask how you ended up there.

Okay, what happened was that I had taken auditions for different schools. I tried Eastman, which I totally messed up. And Manhattan School of Music for some reason I took the theory, to be a theory major. And a student named David Butler had come down to the Music and Art and had talked up Fredonia. So there were about six of us from Music and Art, decided we’d look it up, you know, see what’s up. So I had gotten my teacher because she never was really hot on like Bach. And somehow I felt like I needed to learn…

had already failed Eastman, I wasn’t too happy about New York College of Music and Manhattan School of Music because I felt I’d see myself at the clubs all night with a midterm the next day. Because I’d probably be at the clubs watching Milt Jackson or Herbie, instead of studying for an exam. So I said I need to get out of New York. So I finished the audition and he says, “Well Allan, you know there aren’t many black people in Fredonia.” My thing was I really don’t care, I want to know did I pass the audition or…

items.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: And the benefit of that is that there is a club called the Revelot, and all the cats came through. ... Herbie and Ahmad Jamal, Rahsaan Roland Kirk... So that was pretty cool. So I had sown the seeds for the future by meeting all these cats that I was able to talk to and get to know

ctx.x: I had passed through Buffalo but I’d never stayed in Buffalo. So I met some musicians during that time and he called me and said we have a program, we’d like you to teach, it’s a Model Cities program. And it turned out that this program fit the requirements of a CO deferment. Because it had to be a nonprofit organization, more than fifty miles away from your home base. Voila. So I started working right away. I didn’t wait for them to assign © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -9-

me, I just started working. And they wrote the person who was in charge, Sabu signed a form, I had to send away to show what I was making and all that kind of stuff. So about six months later I get reclassified. So I’m relieved of my CO classification, but in other words you’ll never be called. You don’t have to do service anymore and don’t worry about being called. But since I was working up there in Buffalo and getting paid, and going through this whole thing with the music and the culture and everything, I…
